text: Agile values useful documentation not the elimination of documentation
We will examine stories criteria cases defects charters and
traceability Imagine joining a team just before release The
invoice feature looks finished but nobody can explain which
account-isolation checks ran or which build contains the last
fix More documents would not automatically solve the problem
Useful artifacts would connect the customer need expected behavior
and evidence Agile values working software while still recognizing
that documentation can support collaboration and decisions In this
lesson we create a small connected set of artifacts
for a monthly invoice download Every artifact should answer
a practical question for someone who needs to understand
verify operate or change the product
A customer wants to download a monthly invoice Clarify
completed billing periods P D F output and account
ownership Acceptance criteria translate the need into verifiable outcomes
Write the user story in terms of the customer
goal a customer wants to download a monthly invoice
to keep a record of charges Then clarify the
acceptance criteria Only completed billing periods are available the
output is a readable P D F and customers
can access only their own invoices Add an example
of a month with no charge if the business
needs it Criteria should describe observable outcomes rather than
merely repeat interface labels A story that says there
is a Download button is incomplete if it never
explains which document the button must retrieve or who
is allowed to retrieve it
A test case can specify ID objective precondition action
and expected result For invoice downloads verify that an
authenticated customer downloads the correct P D F Use
detailed cases for high-risk work and checklists where sufficient
Create one test case with enough detail for its
risk Its identifier is INV zero one The precondition
is a synthetic customer with a completed billing period
and a known invoice The action is to request
that period's download The expected result is the correct
P D F with the agreed account and charge
information Record the environment and build when executing it
A second test should investigate access to another synthetic
customer's invoice Detailed steps are useful where precision matters
but a simple low-risk visual check may only need
a checklist Match the detail to the reader's need
and the consequences of ambiguity
An invoice ID modification that exposes another customer’s file
is a serious authorization issue Record environment steps expected
and actual behavior and sanitized evidence Avoid exposing sensitive
customer data Suppose modifying the invoice identifier returns another
account's document Write a defect that explains the authorization
failure without exposing real customer information Include the environment
synthetic account relationship reproduction steps and observed result State
the expected denial and attach sanitized evidence Link the
affected requirement and test Avoid putting access tokens or
confidential invoices in a broadly shared ticket The report
should help the team reproduce and prioritize the problem
not create a second exposure After the fix retain
enough retest evidence to show which build was checked
and what outcome was observed
A lightweight strategy documents scope risks environments responsibilities and
automation An exploratory charter might focus on invoice downloads
across roles and billing periods Capture observations afterward A
one-page strategy can describe scope important risks environments responsibilities
and the mix of automated and human checks For
this feature highlight account isolation document accuracy and availability
Add an exploratory charter investigate invoice access across roles
and billing periods using synthetic accounts A charter sets
a mission while leaving room to follow discoveries After
the session capture what was covered what was found
and what remains uncertain This is more useful than
a long plan copied from an unrelated project that
nobody updates or uses when making a release decision
Link authorization requirements to tests defects fixes and retest
evidence This helps teams demonstrate coverage especially in regulated
environments without unnecessary bureaucracy Traceability can be lightweight Connect
the account-ownership rule to the unauthorized-download check Link the
failing result to the defect then the fix and
retest Someone reviewing release readiness can follow that chain
and understand why the risk is considered addressed The
same principle applies to automated results retain the build
and relevant report rather than only a screenshot of
a green badge Avoid maintaining multiple disconnected copies of
the same relationship in spreadsheets and tickets A small
set of current links is easier to trust than
a large matrix that stopped reflecting the product several
sprints ago
Maintain stories criteria risk strategy important tests defect reports
automated results and relevant release notes Keep artifacts accessible
and current Decide what to keep current Stories and
criteria describe the agreed behavior Important tests preserve repeatable
checks Defect reports record actionable failures Automated reports show
what ran on a build Operational notes explain relevant
deployment or support concerns Release notes communicate changes to
their intended audience Each artifact has a different reader
and lifespan When behavior changes identify which artifacts now
contain an obsolete rule Documentation debt grows when old
expectations remain easy to find but hard to distinguish
from current guidance Prefer concise material with clear ownership
and a visible relationship to the implementation
For your exercise create a miniature evidence chain for
the invoice authorization defect Write one criterion one negative
test a concise defect title and a retest note
The criterion restricts downloads to the owning customer The
test attempts access from a different synthetic account The
defect states that the file was returned The retest
note identifies the fixed build and the observed denial
Explain why a screenshot alone would be insufficient if
it omitted the account context and build Useful documentation
allows another person to reconstruct the decision without needing
the original tester to explain every missing detail
Review a bad test case click Download and verify
the invoice is correct It leaves correctness undefined Improve
it by naming the synthetic account billing period expected
document identity and important fields Record which build and
environment were used Now another tester can tell whether
the file belongs to the right account and period
rather than simply confirming that a P D F
opened Do not add irrelevant detail such as every
pointer movement if it does not help reproducibility Precision
should serve the risk and the reader A concise
test with an observable expected result can be more
useful than pages of mechanical steps with an ambiguous
conclusion
Documentation also needs maintenance when the product changes Suppose
invoices become available on the first business day after
a billing period instead of immediately at its end
Update the acceptance examples automated expectations relevant support guidance
and any checks that rely on the previous availability
rule Record the change where the team will look
for current behavior An obsolete test can create noise
while an obsolete customer-facing explanation can create confusion Assign
ownership to the artifact that matters and remove redundant
copies where possible Keeping a small set of documents
current is usually more useful than creating a large
collection whose readers cannot identify the authoritative version
Documentation should help teams understand and decide Knowledge check
what details make a defect reproducible Subscribe to Tech

share the most important risk you identified in the
